result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Answer A meets nearly every rubric item. It uses labels, an email type with autocapitalize and spellcheck off, current-password, a single one-time-code field with numeric inputmode, a 'Sign in' button, and it removes the script. Its autocomplete on the email field is 'username' rather than 'email', which is a minor miss. Answer B does not turn off autocapitalize or autocorrect on the email field, and it uses a generic 'Log in'. It also keeps the code field in the same form as the password, but that is acceptable. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B meets every rubric item: visible labels, an email type with autocapitalize and spellcheck off, current-password, a single one-time-code field with numeric input mode, 'Sign in', and no script. A lacks autocapitalize and autocorrect settings on the email field, and its 'Log in' button is acceptable but less specific. B also splits the flow into two steps and adds a show-password button, which is scope creep and leaves a script unwritten, but it is still the stronger answer on the rubric.
